Guide & Academy/BA Lending Academy/Module 9

Module 9 of 15

Compliance operations, data and AI governance

Proving it: the audit spine, the reporting duties, the data rules and the machines under command.

Everything earlier in this course produces evidence; this module is about operating that evidence. The audit hash chain and evidence packs, the credit-information reporting cadence, data residency and DPDP operations, and the model/AI governance a BA must be able to explain to an auditor.

4 lessons65 min guided timeComplete in sequence

Lesson 9.1 · 16 min

The audit spine: hash chain and evidence packs

  • Explain the append-only, hash-chained audit record and tamper evidence
  • Describe what an evidence pack is and how exports stay governed
  • Connect audit lineage to decision replay

Lesson 9.2 · 15 min

Credit information reporting: the fortnightly duty

  • State the UCRF reporting cadence and repair clocks
  • Explain borrower-facing duties: alerts, corrections, compensation
  • See where reporting sits in LoanOS

Lesson 9.3 · 16 min

Data operations: residency, retention and DPDP in practice

  • Apply the India-residency rules per data class
  • Operate retention, deletion and legal hold coherently
  • Handle breach duties: DPDP, CERT-In and RBI clocks together

Lesson 9.4 · 18 min

Model risk and AI governance: the full picture

  • Run a model's lifecycle: inventory → validation → activation → monitoring → retirement
  • Explain digital-worker governance: proposal-only agents, guardrails, human approval
  • Brief an auditor on AI controls without hand-waving
